extracted.intended_audience: public company issuers, corporate counsel, CFOs, investor_relations and SEC_filing teams
extracted.subtask_short: Reg S-K MD&A financial disclosure compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and compliance requirements for Regulation S-K financial and MD&A disclosure (Items 301, 302, 303) applicable to U.S. public companies and certain other filers, describing what must be disclosed, thresholds, and presentation expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selected Financial Data (Item 301) — elimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Eliminated: the requirement to provide selected financial data in comparative tabular form for each of the company's last five fiscal years (along with any additional fiscal years necessary to prevent the information from being misleading).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This item was eliminated because prior period financial disclosures are easily accessible through prior EDGAR filings. Companies may voluntarily elect to provide disclosure consistent with an amended item so long as they provide disclosure that follows the amended item in its entirety and in any applicable filings going forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selected Quarterly Financial Data (Item 302(a)) — disclosure only for retrospective material changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies are required to disclose quarterly financial data only when there are one or more retrospective changes that pertain to the statements of comprehensive income for any of the quarters within the two most recent fiscal years and any subsequent interim period and that, individually or in the aggregate, are material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, Item 302(a) requires disclosure beginning with the first filing of Form 10-K after the company's IPO. For newly public companies with a material retrospective change to year-to-date interim period information not previously disclosed in quarterly increments, the SEC will not object if Item 302(a) disclosures are presented for the affected year-to-date interim period and fourth quarter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selected Quarterly Financial Data — explanation and summarized information when required
rubrics_metrics.description: When Item 302(a) applies due to retrospective material changes, companies must provide an explanation of the reasons for such material changes and disclose, for each affected quarterly period and the fourth quarter in the affected year, summarized financial information related to the statements of comprehensive income and earnings per share reflecting such changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amended rule points to Rule 1-02(bb) of Regulation S-X to specify the summarized financial information required; Rule 1-02(bb) was amended to clarify that the disclosure of summary financial information may vary, as appropriate, to conform to the nature of the company's business.

rubrics_metrics.name: MD&A Objective (new Item 303(a)) — focus MD&A on material disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: New Item 303(a) is intended to encourage companies to tailor MD&A disclosure to their specific business and focus on disclosing trends and information that are material. Companies are required to discuss and analyze: material information relevant to an assessment of financial condition and results of operations (including amounts and certainty of cash flows); material events and uncertainties known to management that are reasonably likely to cause reported financial information not to be indicative of future results; and material financial and statistical data that enhance a reader's understanding of financial condition, cash flows, and results of operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This codifies guidance that MD&A should provide a narrative that enables investors to see the company 'through the eyes of management.' The focus is principles-based and tailored to what is material to the company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full Fiscal Years MD&A (Item 303(b)) — discussion of financial condition and results
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must discuss financial condition, changes in financial condition, and results of operations for full fiscal years, including topics identified (liquidity, capital resources, results of operations, off-balance sheet arrangements, and contractual obligations) and other information necessary to understand financial condition and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where appropriate, discussion should focus on each relevant reportable segment and/or other subdivisions (e.g., geographic areas); product lines are explicitly identified as a type of subdivision that may be necessary to discuss based on management judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain reasons underlying material changes (quantitative and qualitative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should not only discuss the 'cause' for material changes but also the reasons underlying material changes in quantitative and qualitative terms. The rule codifies that causes for year-to-year material changes in line items must be described and that discussion includes when material changes within a line item offset one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC recognizes that isolating and quantifying reasons can be challenging due to interrelated factors; in such cases, companies are encouraged to acknowledge interrelationships and explain them to the extent possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liquidity and Capital Resources analysis (Item 303(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: New Item 303(b)(1) requires an overarching analysis of a company's ability to generate and obtain adequate cash to meet requirements and plans for cash in the short term (next 12 months) and separately in the long term (beyond next 12 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New Instruction 3 to Item 303(b) provides that the analysis should be in a format that facilitates easy understanding and should supplement, but not duplicate, disclosure already provided in the filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose material cash requirements (contractual obligations table eliminated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should analyze material cash requirements from known contractual and other obligations (rather than only material commitments for capital expenditures) and specify the type of obligation and the relevant time period for related cash requirements. The prior requirement to provide a contractual obligations table (Item 303(a)(5)) has been eliminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction 4 to Item 303(b) gives examples of material cash requirements that may be discussed, such as lease obligations, purchase obligations, or other liabilities reflected on the balance sheet. This codifies prior SEC guidance and should not substantially change current practice regarding assessment of material cash requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trends/uncertainties impacting continuing operations — 'reasonably likely' threshold (Item 303(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: New Item 303(b)(2)(ii) provides that when a company knows of events that are 'reasonably likely' to cause a material impact on net sales, revenues, or income from continuing operations (or a material change in the relationship between costs and revenues), those changes must be disclosed. Whether a change is reasonably likely is based on management's assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The change to the 'reasonably likely' threshold aligns Item 303 with other disclosure thresholds; the adopting release reiterates that the analysis should be based on materiality and what a reasonable investor would consider important, and calls on companies to make a thoughtful, objective assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results of operations — discuss both increases and decreases in net sales/revenues
rubrics_metrics.description: A results of operations discussion should describe not only increases but also decreases in net sales or revenues, including the extent to which such changes are attributable to price, volume, or new products/services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a recaptioned and amended continuation of prior requirements to give a balanced discussion of directional changes in revenues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inflation/price changes reference removed to avoid boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: The specific reference to discussing the impact of inflation and price changes was removed from Item 303 because it could lead to undue attention and boilerplate disclosures; however, if inflation or price changes are part of a known trend or uncertainty that is material or reasonably likely to be material, they must still be discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal is intended to reduce formulaic disclosures and encourage focus on material trends and uncertainties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Off-balance sheet arrangements — integrate into MD&A (Instruction 8 to Item 303(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Rather than requiring a separately captioned section, companies must discuss off-balance sheet arrangements in the broader MD&A, even when the arrangement does not result in an obligation reported in the consolidated balance sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change reflects overlap with U.S. GAAP note disclosures and the SEC's move from prescriptive requirements toward principles-based MD&A instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim periods comparisons (Item 303(c)) — flexibility to compare sequential quarters
rubrics_metrics.description: New Item 303(c) permits companies to compare their most recently completed quarter's results of operations to either the corresponding quarter of the prior year or the immediately preceding quarter, allowing flexibility to tailor analysis to business cycles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a company elects the immediately preceding quarter comparison, it must provide summary financial information for that quarter or identify the prior EDGAR filing that presents such information. If a company later changes the comparison approach in a subsequent Form 10-Q, it must explain the reason for the change and present both comparisons in the filing where the change is announced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical accounting estimates (Item 303(b)(3)) — disclose estimation uncertainty and sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must disclose critical accounting estimates defined as GAAP estimates involving significant estimation uncertainty that have had or are reasonably likely to have a material impact on financial condition or results of operations. Disclosure should provide qualitative and quantitative information necessary to understand the estimation uncertainty and the impact each critical accounting estimate has had or is reasonably likely to have.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure should include why each estimate is subject to uncertainty, how much each estimate/assumption has changed over a relevant period, and the sensitivity of the reported amount to the methods, assumptions, and estimates underlying its calculation. Such disclosure should supplement, not duplicate, accounting policy descriptions in the financial statement notes.
